citations.review_text:
The Henry Stickmin Collection is basically a playable cartoon where every decision you make has a 50% chance of being genius and a 50% chance of getting Henry killed in the funniest way imaginable.

The games are built around simple choices, but the amount of ridiculous outcomes is what makes them so entertaining. You can attempt elaborate plans, use completely useless items, or make a decision that seems reasonable and immediately discover why it was a terrible idea.

The humor is easily the highlight. The references, animations, characters, and absurd failure scenes make even losing feel like a reward.

There's also a surprising amount of content. Finding all the endings, achievements, and hidden references gives you plenty of reasons to replay the episodes.

It's short, hilarious, and incredibly easy to pick up.

**10/10 — chose the obviously correct option, immediately got launched into the sun.**

[h2]Love Cartoon Violence? Then you'll love Henry Stickmin![/h2]

Henry Stickmin was great in the heyday of the Newgrounds flash game era. This remaster/remake of the games is quite good. If you like cartoons and choose your own adventure genre then you'll most assuredly enjoy the Henry Stickmin Collection. It may also have an appeal to fans of the point and click genre.

It contains hours of making the wrong choices and that's the fun part! Your choices shape what happens and lead to several different endings. It also contains timed choices where you only have a few seconds to decide.

It's silly but fun.

[h2]8/10[/h2]

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that the game lacks a feature to skip cutscenes that have already been seen.

citations.review_text:
This game is great, as it features loads of little easter eggs to different games - my favourites of which are in Fleeing The Complex and Completing The Mission (stuff like the BotW stamina wheel and finding a ledge to replenish some, or the opening straight out of MGS 3 when you pick the Rapidly Promoted Exec + Presumed Dead). I love the attention to detail. This only ramps up in CTM, which is extremely ambitious - it accounts for the different endings that you got in ITA and FTC, letting your choices influence whether you go after the train, rocket or satellite. 

My only real complaint about the game is that you're unable to skip cutscenes, or at least ones that you have seen 2+ times. I wouldn't mind if you were only able to skip a select few long ones (that aren't timed and don't rely on interaction), but it makes achievement hunting increasingly arduous, having to wait 15 seconds every time you fail to right-click a character who appears for a split second on screen as the camera pans away from them at mach speed (in order to gain their character bio). 

With all that said, I thoroughly enjoyed the game and just wish it was longer, but I can acknowledge that Henry's story is over, with the final instalment aptly being titled "Completing The Mission". 

I knew of this game a long time ago, right next to Riddle School in my childhood. This was a while before I bought it, only remembering it because I saw it on sale. I knew of it because of YouTubers like DanTDM and their Let's Plays of it. ★★★★★

I feel like most people have played or seen at least one iteration of the Henry Stickmin games and if not then youre seriously missing out. Such a charming game that stretched from 2008 - 2020 and came with it one of the best comedy flash games ever. Its an incredibly quick and easy 100% with a lot of fun gameplay, whilst it is on the shorter side and i quite literally beat the game to 100% completion in not even 8 hours. Its still such a blast to see the choices you can make and all the fails and outcomes

Overall for its price of 8.99nzd on sale its more than worth it, Especially if you played this as a kid. Not suuuuper amount of replayability. However for a 100% its honestly not terrrrrrrrible besides the last mission for Bios. Anyway its a great game give it a go

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features remastered visuals for the older titles alongside content changes made due to copyright.

citations.review_text: I remember seeing my favorite YouTuber play through the old Henry Stickmin games and when I found that there was this collection, I knew I wanted to get it, and I don't regret it. The series is extremely fun to play, although on the outside it seems repetitive, making a blind choice and seeing if it works or not, the way each death is unique and how absurd the story can go through sometimes makes up for it. I really liked how Completing the Mission was able to relate back to the other stories and the remastered visuals for the older games look really good. Although you can tell which games were made first with the length of each one, they are all still really good and the game can offer a decent amount of choice with which ending you try to get. The game also has a lot of references to memes in the internet which I think is cool and nostalgic (god I'm old already). Anyways, this game is really good and I think you should get it.

A great ending to the Henry Stickmin series. Glad to see all the games remastered, especially because of the convenience, though it's sad that some things had to be changed because of copyright. The introduction of the bio system is interesting, and gives a reason to replay some of the endings (though it is sometimes hard to get the bios of people that appear on screen for like 1 second). Overall I really enjoyed the game(s), mostly because of the humor, but also because it's just interesting to follow Henry's story
